subject: Notice: EdgeSight telemetry processor onboarding & DPA addendum
messages:
From: EdgeSight Onboarding <onboarding@edgesight.com>

Cc: Grace Lee <grace.lee@greenline.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeSight onboarding: telemetry processing & DPA addendum

Hi Kimberly,

As part of our upcoming pilot with Greenline, we need to notify Redwood Inference of a delegated processor that will handle runtime telemetry and aggregated telemetry logs. EdgeSight will act as a telemetry relay/cache for a subset of non-customer PII (hashed connection ids, timestamps, latency metrics). We are submitting a DPA addendum and evidence package for review.

Attachments included: EdgeSight_DPA_Addendum_v1.pdf; edgesight-soc2-report-2027.pdf; edgesight-dataflow.png.

High-level notes:
- Processing scope: telemetry only (no model input retention beyond short-lived traces).
- Geographic processing: US primary, EU backup for GDPR projects (subject to routing rules).
- Encryption: data at rest encrypted with AES-256; transit TLS 1.2+.

Request: please confirm whether this subprocessor addition is acceptable under Redwood's controls and list any evidence you need for Greenline to proceed. We are live next week for a limited pilot window and would appreciate a quick turn.

Thanks,
Ravi Kapoor
Onboarding Manager
EdgeSight

Ravi —

Thanks for the heads up and the documents. A few quick clarifying asks from our side to speed review: 

1) Can you confirm the exact fields you will see (schema) and whether any hashed identifiers are reversible by EdgeSight?
2) SOC2: do you have a current SOC2 Type II report; if not, can you provide the assessment date and scope?
3) Data residency: confirm whether EU telemetry will be stored in an EU region and whether we can pin routing per-customer (Greenline) to onshore nodes.
4) Retention: what is your default retention for traces and cache entries, and is there a TTL override for customers with stricter retention requirements?

For now I am CC'ing Marissa and Jordan for legal/controls review. Marissa — can you advise whether the DPA addendum, plus the SOC2 report, and the dataflow diagram are sufficient for an expedited approval? If not, list the minimal additional evidence we need to ask EdgeSight for.

We will treat this as impact-to-data-subprocessors and aim to turn within 48 hours if possible.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Vendor Risk
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeSight onboarding: telemetry processing & DPA addendum

Hi Kimberly et al.,

Thanks — answers inline below and attached are the requested documents.

1) Field schema: we will receive only aggregated telemetry tuples: {timestamp, latency_ms, route_hash, error_flag, region_code}. route_hash is HMAC-SHA256 keyed per-customer; keys are not reversible by EdgeSight.
2) SOC2: attaching our SOC2 Type II report (edgesight-soc2-report-2027.pdf). Assessment period: Jan–Dec 2027, control scope includes secure configuration, change management, logging, and access controls.
3) Residency: default is US. For Greenline, we can pin routing to EU nodes; the dataflow diagram shows conditional routing based on customer tag.
4) Retention: default 90 days; we support TTL overrides down to 7 days upon contractual agreement.

Additional notes: We do not persist raw model inputs or customer prompts. Cache entries contain only hashed route_ids and telemetry; encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).

Forwarding for your review; DocuSign link for DPA addendum: https://docusign.com/recipient/AAABBB-edgesight-12345

Best,
Ravi Kapoor
Onboarding Manager
EdgeSight

Subject: Fwd: EdgeSight onboarding: telemetry processing & DPA addendum

Kim/Marissa/Ben —

Quick legal summary after reviewing the materials:

- DPA addendum is acceptable with two clarifying edits (non-subordination of liability clause and narrow definition of telemetry). I'll propose redline language — see inline suggestions in the draft.
- SOC2 report is current and within scope; evidence of monitoring and key management is adequate.
- Residency and TTL: EdgeSight has the capability to pin routing and shorten retention to 7 days; we should require those as options in the SOW for Greenline.

Recommendation: approve the subprocessor before the pilot on the following conditions:
1) EdgeSight signs the DPA addendum with our redlines (I will send redline via DocuSign).
2) Greenline is given an explicit routing pin to EU for their EU workloads; Redwood will enforce routing tag on request.
3) For any workloads that require <30 day retention, a customer-specific SLA/T&Cs checklist will be attached to the DPA.

Marissa — please confirm if you want to send the acceptance + conditional list to Greenline directly or have me/Ben do that.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
